text:
- chief complaint: hypogonadism follow-up, with the patient also concerned about gynecomastia.
- history of present illness: the patient is a 59-year-old male with HIV, last seen 2020-11-24, on testosterone therapy (1 mL every 10 days) for hypogonadism. Baseline testosterone was under 300. Currently taking finasteride 5 mg (half tablet) and tadalafil (Cialis) 2.5 mg or 5 mg depending on workout days, with a recent lapse in tadalafil. Latest PSA is 0.6 and testosterone is above 1,500. Triglycerides fell from 265 to 145 mg/dL in about 5 months since starting testosterone.
- physical examination: heart and lung exam normal.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: feels well, more vigorous, sleeps well; no physical body changes noted by patient. N/A for other symptoms.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A. The patient requested refills of tadalafil and finasteride, with a paper prescription; the doctor agreed to send them. Testosterone dose unchanged.
- follow-up instructions: keep testosterone dose unchanged; PSA and testosterone checked about once a year; the doctor will send prescriptions.
